issue.title: [Bug]: This module cannot be imported from a Client Component module. It should only be used from a Server Component.
issue.body:
### Version

29.4.3

### Steps to reproduce

Create any component and add the `import "server-only"` (https://www.npmjs.com/package/server-only) to mark it as server only code.

Try to run any test against it and they are going to fail and log the following message: 

```This module cannot be imported from a Client Component module. It should only be used from a Server Component.```

### Expected behavior

The test(s) should be able to run without any issues.

### Actual behavior

Test fail and log 

```This module cannot be imported from a Client Component module. It should only be used from a Server Component.```

### Additional context

I've already tried the following:

1. New project on jest.config with `testEnvironment: 'node'`
2. Environment comment on test file 
```
/**
 * @jest-environment node
 */
 ```

### Environment

```shell
System:
    OS: macOS 12.5.1
    CPU: (16) x64 Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-9880H CPU @ 2.30GHz
  Binaries:
    Node: 18.12.1 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v18.12.1/bin/node
    npm: 8.19.2 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v18.12.1/bin/npm
  npmPackages:
    jest: ^29.4.3 => 29.4.3
```

body: Same issue. Would love to start testing :) Or would I......

> Related to #47299

In that issue the explanation is that `@testing-library/react` simulates a browser, but I get that error also without that library. I was trying to test some logic that doesn't uses React and should always run on the server.

It's more that `jsdom` simulates a browser (a client), I think. That must trigger some Next.js or React code that checks to see if a React Sever Component is being used outside of a Server context.

The NEXT-889 issue tag in the issue title means that the Next team are tracking this internally, so that's a good sign.

I think one solution will be to have two Jest ~~profiles~~ projects, one for client-side code and one for server-side code. With two ~~profiles~~ projects you can have two different environments, `jsdom` for the client and then Node for the server.
A seperate profile is a good idea. Do you have an example that works with Nextjs 13 maybe?

> A seperate profile is a good idea. Do you have an example that works with Nextjs 13 maybe?

No, sorry, not yet.

My team was about to start looking into it but then I saw that Vercel had updated this ticket with a Linear/Jira ticket reference, so we put the idea to the side and will wait for an official docs update.

If you'd like an example of using two Jest profiles then I think the 'Next Right Now' repo has an example of it. I'm on my phone at the moment but will post this comment then go and find and share a URL on my laptop…

Ah, I was wrong, it was Blitz, not 'Next Right Now': https://github.com/blitz-js/blitz/blob/canary/packages/blitz/jest-preset.js#L50-L82

Someone has also shared an example of using ~~profiles~~ projects (I got the name wrong in my earlier comment) here: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/12411#discussioncomment-5472457

Ah yeah, `server-only` does some stuff that won't be affected by just the `jsdom` vs `node` environment switch.

https://github.com/facebook/jest/issues/13967 has some info on this. There are two things we can try (I've not tried these yet, so not sure if they actually work):

Mocking `server-only`, potentially?: https://github.com/facebook/jest/issues/13967#issuecomment-1468987614

Someone else pointed out how `server-only` works (`package.json` exports, with the error being thrown only if the `react-server` export is _not_ used), and suggested how to override what export is used in Jest: https://github.com/facebook/jest/issues/13967#issuecomment-1493284963
Confirming this also affects me. The 'Testing' section of the app beta docs is still greyed out / unpublished, so hopefully a solution is in the pipes.

issue.title: Refactor API endpoints into Server Actions
issue.body:
https://github.com/nimblehq/js-framework-benchmark/pull/106#discussion_r1220630242

## What happened 👀
- Add [the new actions.tsx file](https://github.com/nimblehq/js-framework-benchmark/pull/129/files#diff-ea081786071108e74c9128ec18214e4b25464c487e41f4f3cf2961361d3a9b8a) to contains all actions for 4 Server Actions(Create, Update, Delete, Send)
- Modify client code to use Server Actions instead of calling APIs
- Add and modify tests
- Remove all the API codes and tests of 4 actions

## Insight 📝
### Purpose of PR
As discussed [here](https://github.com/nimblehq/js-framework-benchmark/pull/106#discussion_r1220630242), this is the PR to refactor all the API code that can be replaced by [Next.js Server Actions](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/data-fetching/server-actions).

### API to Server Actions
It's surprising for me to see that it's very easy to refactor a flow that's using API to using Server Action in Next.js v13.

For example, for this sending newsletter feature, to use Server Action, based [on the refactored code here](https://github.com/nimblehq/js-framework-benchmark/pull/129/files#diff-1410c2c61c8257ce65caa55dcf666a7b6315edc7ddd9c166d4b608a8fe552feb), we just need to:
- Replace the `axios` call without our server action(the function `sendNewsletter` in this example)
- Wrap the whole calling server action thing in [`startTransition`](https://github.com/nimblehq/js-framework-benchmark/pull/129/files#diff-1410c2c61c8257ce65caa55dcf666a7b6315edc7ddd9c166d4b608a8fe552febR50)(`startTransition` is 1 of the 3 ways to use Server Action in Nextjs, along with [`action`](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/data-fetching/server-actions#action) and [`formAction`](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/data-fetching/server-actions#formaction))
- Everything else stays the same

### Cons
It is easy to use this new Server Action feature, but since this is still a new feature, there are some difficulties I faced while trying it, such as:
- [Not very compatible with `NextAuth`](https://github.com/nextauthjs/next-auth/issues/7486)(when try to get user session on server side, NextAuth raise errors), but luckily, there is [this work around](https://github.com/nextauthjs/next-auth/issues/7486#issuecomment-1543747325)
- When we run tests, it raises some [import errors](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/47448#issuecomment-1483028284), resulting in having to do a lot of import mock like [this](https://github.com/nimblehq/js-framework-benchmark/pull/129/files#diff-4b9ae30a4e34a98e0e0d12af3e4872e7ac9865c68f016c1e6667d4336ce08ce1R16-R21) to make it works.
- It also raises errors when running tests if we import server actions from a file that has "use server" to test files. So instead of only having 2 file, `actions/newsletter.tsx`, I have to create a new [`actions/actions.tsx`](https://github.com/nimblehq/js-framework-benchmark/pull/129/files#diff-ea081786071108e74c9128ec18214e4b25464c487e41f4f3cf2961361d3a9b8a) file that contains the server actions but not the "use server", and when I need to use the server actions on client components, I use it through this [`actions/newsletter.tsx`](https://github.com/nimblehq/js-framework-benchmark/pull/129/files#diff-c4535b6fc32b017b9c90ca00f3e5baaa01f19f24913e5725a69319a7376c512a)(which only to import actions from `actions.tsx` AND ADD the "use server").

### Refs
- This is a very easy to understand introduction about Server Actions: [Next.js Server Actions... 5 awesome things you can do](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O94ESaJtHtM&ab_channel=BeyondFireship&themeRefresh=1)

## Proof Of Work 📹
`N/A`

[Testing](https://nextjs.org/docs/pages/building-your-application/optimizing/testing)

There is no corresponding page in the _Using Apps Router_ section

It would be really helpful to have such a page for people using the Apps Router documentation (even if it is a pointer back to the same content).

```
Cannot find module 'private-next-rsc-action-proxy' from 'src/actions/LibraryActions.ts'
```

(LibraryActions.ts is a bunch of server actions talking to the library database, with "use server" at the top.)

I do not know if there is something weird in my Jest setup, or if that is an actual issue.


### Does the docs page already exist? Please link to it.

_No response_

issue.title: fix(next/jest): jest can not load server-only code
issue.body:
### 🧐 What's in there? At the moment, it is not possible to test code with `import 'server-only'` in app directory. When trying to load such file in jest (even with `testEnvironment: node`), the error will be: ``` ● Test suite failed to run·· x NEXT_RSC_ERR_CLIENT_IMPORT: server-only ,-[lib/util.js:1:1] 1 | /** @jest-environment node */· 2 | import 'server-only' : ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ 3 | export const PI = 3.14; `----· at Object.transformSync (node_modules/next/src/build/swc/index.ts:443:25) at transformSync (node_modules/next/src/build/swc/index.ts:629:19) at Object.process (node_modules/next/src/build/swc/jest-transformer.ts:117:25) at ScriptTransformer.transformSource (node_modules/@jest/transform/build/ScriptTransformer.js:619:31) at ScriptTransformer._transformAndBuildScript (node_modules/@jest/transform/build/ScriptTransformer.js:765:40) at ScriptTransformer.transform (node_modules/@jest/transform/build/ScriptTransformer.js:822:19)· ``` In a nutshell: - next/swc is looking for ‘server-only’ [text in the source](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next-swc/crates/core/src/react_server_components.rs#L576), and throw if not configured for server - next's jest-transformer will only configure next/swc for server [if the environment is node](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/src/build/swc/jest-transformer.ts#L88) - when testing Next.js apps, your jest testEnvironment is most likely jsdom. But you can configure it [per file with docBlock](https://jestjs.io/docs/configuration#testenvironment-string), which jest-transformer ignores because it only reads the top-level configuration. This PR fixes this, by 1. reading the docblock to configure next/swc accordingly and bypass its hardcoded guard 2. mocking `server-only` so [it does not throw](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/src/compiled/server-only/index.js) when loaded (jest does not read `react-server` export from package.json) Users would still have to annotate their `server-only` files with `/** @jest-environment node */` in order to test them. ### 🧪 How to test? There's a full test available: `pnpm testheadless --testPathPattern jest/server-only` Here is also a minimal reproduction:
app/layout.tsx ```typescript export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { return ({children}) } ```
app/page.tsx ```typescript import { PI } from '@/lib/utils' export default function Home() { return

{PI}

} ```
lib/utils.ts ```typescript import 'server-only' export const PI = 3.14 ```
lib/utils.test.ts ```typescript import { PI } from './utils' it('works', () => expect(PI).toEqual(3.14)) ```
jest.config.js ```typescript const nextJest = require('next/jest') module.exports = nextJest({ dir: './' })({ testEnvironment: 'jsdom' }) ```
### ❗ Notes to reviewers [jest-docblock](https://packagephobia.com/result?p=jest-docblock) with dependencies is only 12.5 kB. Fixes #47448
